questions.question: The four figures to memorise for dry air by volume are:
options: Nitrogen 78%, oxygen 21%, argon 0,93%, carbon dioxide 0,04%
Oxygen 78%, nitrogen 21%, carbon dioxide 0,93%
Nitrogen 60%, oxygen 40%
Nitrogen 78%, water vapour 21%, oxygen 0,93%

questions.question: Water vapour, dust and ozone are grouped together because they are:
options: The heaviest gases in the atmosphere
VARIABLE components — their amounts change with place and time, unlike the permanent gases nitrogen, oxygen and argon
All produced only by human activity
Found only above the tropopause

questions.question: Nitrogen earns its place in the atmosphere by:
options: Absorbing ultraviolet radiation in the stratosphere
Reflecting radio waves back to earth
DILUTING oxygen so burning stays manageable, and supplying the stock that soil bacteria fix into nitrates for plant proteins
Producing thunderstorm electricity

questions.question: Without dust and other aerosols in the air:
options: The sky would turn green
Air pressure would rise sharply
Photosynthesis would stop
Cloud droplets would struggle to form, because each speck is a CONDENSATION NUCLEUS onto which cooling water vapour condenses

subtopics.title: The Four Layers — Structure by Temperature

questions.question: The single test used to divide the atmosphere into its four layers is:
options: Whether temperature rises or falls as altitude increases
How much oxygen each layer contains
The strength of the wind in each layer
The height of the clouds

questions.question: Hikers on Thabana Ntlenyana can stand in sleet while the valley below is warm because the troposphere:
options: Contains no water vapour at altitude
Is heated FROM BELOW by long-wave radiation off the ground, so air cools by about 6,5 °C per 1 000 m of climb
Is heated by ozone at its top
Has stronger sunshine at the bottom

questions.question: Long-haul aircraft cruise in the lower stratosphere because:
options: The air there is rich in oxygen for the engines
It is the warmest layer of the atmosphere
Its standing inversion suppresses convection — no rising currents, no cloud, no weather, so the flying is smooth
Radio contact is impossible lower down

questions.question: Shooting stars are evidence of the:
options: Thermosphere reflecting sunlight
Stratosphere absorbing ultraviolet
Tropopause blocking rising air
MESOSPHERE — meteoroids burn up in its thin air, below the mesopause at about −90 °C, the coldest point in the atmosphere

subtopics.title: The Ozone Layer — Shield, Damage and Repair

questions.question: Compressed to surface pressure, the entire ozone layer would form a sheet about:
options: Three millimetres deep — yet it absorbs nearly all incoming ultraviolet-B and ultraviolet-C
Three hundred metres deep
Thirty centimetres deep
Three kilometres deep

questions.question: Industry originally embraced CFCs because they seemed harmless; that same stability is dangerous because:
options: It makes them explode at altitude
Rain cannot remove them, so they drift up for years until stratospheric UV cracks them open and frees chlorine
They freeze into ice crystals near the ground
They react instantly with oxygen at sea level

questions.question: Chlorine attacks ozone CATALYTICALLY, which means:
options: It needs sunlight for every single reaction
It is used up after destroying one molecule
The atom emerges unchanged from each reaction and attacks again, so one atom can destroy tens of thousands of ozone molecules
It converts ozone into carbon dioxide

questions.question: Ozone depletion threatens fisheries off South Africa's Atlantic coast because:
options: It warms the ocean surface
It increases rainfall over the sea
It dissolves into the water as acid
Extra ultraviolet damages PHYTOPLANKTON, the microscopic base of the marine food web that feeds the snoek and sardine stocks

subtopics.title: Why the Atmosphere Matters — and the Exam Method

questions.question: The natural greenhouse effect keeps the earth's average surface temperature at about:
options: 15 °C — without it the figure would fall to about −18 °C
30 °C — without it the figure would be 15 °C
0 °C — without it the figure would be −50 °C
15 °C — without it nothing would change

questions.question: The Moon's surface swings from far above 100 °C to below −150 °C in a single day because it:
options: Is much closer to the sun than the earth
Has no atmosphere to blanket heat in at night or filter radiation by day
Rotates faster than the earth
Is made of darker rock

questions.question: The fastest reliable way to label every layer on a temperature-height graph is to:
options: Memorise the height of each layer
Measure the steepness of the line
Find the TURNING POINTS — each elbow is a pause, and labelling tropopause, stratopause and mesopause places every layer
Start from the top and work down

questions.question: The lesson's terminology warning is that ozone at street level is:
options: Part of the protective shield
Chemically different from stratospheric ozone
Beneficial to crops
A POLLUTANT cooked out of exhaust fumes by sunlight — the same molecule as the shield, judged oppositely because of altitude

questions.question: In the choir of one hundred singers standing for dry air:
options: 78 basses are nitrogen, 21 tenors are oxygen, and one lone singer is everything else
50 basses are nitrogen and 50 tenors are oxygen
78 singers are oxygen and 21 are nitrogen
Every singer is carbon dioxide

questions.question: To represent carbon dioxide honestly you need a stadium of ten thousand singers because:
options: Carbon dioxide is only found in stadiums
Carbon dioxide is roughly FOUR parts in ten thousand of dry air — tiny, yet it feeds plants and holds in warmth
Carbon dioxide makes up ten per cent of air
The choir cannot sing low enough

questions.question: Textbook tables of air composition quietly say 'dry air' at the top because:
options: Nitrogen dissolves in rain
Instruments only work in deserts
WATER VAPOUR swings by the hour — drenched over St Lucia in January, almost absent over Sutherland in July — so it is left out of the fixed recipe
Oxygen evaporates in humid weather

subtopics.title: Four Camps on One Impossible Mountain

questions.question: At base camp — the troposphere — the fire is:
options: The GROUND itself, which soaks up sunshine and breathes warmth back out, so climbing takes you away from the fire and into cold
Hanging above the camp
Missing entirely
Carried by the wind

questions.question: Camp two — the stratosphere — is perfectly still and cloudless because:
options: It contains no gases at all
Its fire hangs ABOVE the camp: warm air resting on cold air is a lid, so nothing rises and no cloud forms
The wind blows straight downward there
It is below freezing everywhere

questions.question: The roof of camp three — the mesopause — is special because it is:
options: The warmest point of the climb
Where all weather happens
The coldest spot on the whole mountain, around −90 °C, in the layer where space gravel burns into shooting stars
Where aircraft cruise

questions.question: A climber at the summit — the thermosphere — would freeze despite readings of thousands of degrees because:
options: The thermometer lies at altitude
The sun never shines there
The heat is trapped below the mesopause
Hardly any molecules remain to carry the heat across to a body

subtopics.title: The Shade Net and the Moth

questions.question: The ozone layer is compared to a farmer's shade net because it:
options: Hangs overhead and takes the sting out of the sun before it reaches what lives below
Keeps birds out of the atmosphere
Holds rain above the clouds
Is made of woven plastic

questions.question: Chlorine is 'a moth that never gets full' because one chlorine atom:
options: Eats a single ozone molecule and stops
Chews through an ozone molecule, comes out untouched, and moves straight to the next — tens of thousands of holes from one atom
Grows larger with every reaction
Turns into ozone after each bite

questions.question: The biggest tear in the net opens above Antarctica each southern spring because:
options: Antarctica produces the most CFCs
The sun is strongest at the South Pole
Winter winds seal the polar air into a closed room where the ozone-destroying chemistry runs wild
Sea ice releases chlorine as it melts

questions.question: The ozone story ends well because the Montreal Protocol:
options: Moved the ozone layer higher
Banned all air travel
Paid farmers to plant more trees
Stopped CFC production worldwide, and the net is measurably re-weaving itself year by year
